title: Contraste lingüístico: 'a diferencia de las demás lenguas' y 'no proceder de'

sections.content: While Castilian, Catalan, Valencian, Galician, and Aranese are all Romance languages derived from Latin ('lenguas romances que proceden del latín'), **el euskera** (or **vasco**) stands out with 'a diferencia de las demás lenguas de España, no procede del latín ni pertenece a la familia indoeuropea' (unlike the other languages of Spain, it does not come from Latin nor belong to the Indo-European family). **El gallego** is co-official in **Galicia** (4 provinces: A Coruña, Lugo, Ourense, Pontevedra), while **el euskera** is co-official in the **País Vasco** and in the Basque-speaking areas of **Navarra**.

items.spanish: El gallego es la lengua propia y cooficial junto con el castellano en Galicia.
items.english: Galician is the own and co-official language alongside Castilian in Galicia.

items.spanish: A diferencia de las demás lenguas de España, el euskera no procede del latín.
items.english: Unlike the other languages of Spain, Basque (Euskera) does not come from Latin.

items.spanish: El euskera es lengua cooficial en el País Vasco y en las zonas vascófonas de Navarra.
items.english: Basque is a co-official language in the Basque Country and in the Basque-speaking areas of Navarre.

sections.content: Key CCSE linguistic question: Which official language in Spain does NOT derive from Latin ('no es una lengua romance')? **El euskera (o vasco)**.
